newsitem.title: USA: GM per-share net hits new record.
newsitem.headline: GM per-share net hits new record.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Wednesday it had second quarter income of $2.68 a share based on its $1-2/3 par value common stock, a company record.

Consolidated net income for the period was $2.1 billion. The figures compare to $1.9 billion or $2.63 a year ago. GM's 1997 second quarter earnings included a negative impact of $490 million from two labor strikes, and one-time gains worth $421 million.

Contributing to the per-share increase was the purchase of 8.3 million shares of $1-2/3 par value common stock worth $469 million that GM made in the second quarter. For the first half of 1997, GM said it used $2 billion to buy back 35.5 million shares of stock. That represents 80 percent of the company's $2.5 billion buyback program.

At the end of the second quarter, GM had cash and marketable securities of $14.9 billion, up from $13 billion at the end of the 1996 second period, and $14.6 billion at the end of the 1997 first quarter.
GM Chairman Jack Smith said in a statement that he would have preferred to avoid the labor strikes.

"But we have to make GM competitive, and we need local labor agreements that are consistent with that objective. We think that's really the only way we can provide the long-term prosperity for our people and the unions that represent them, as well as our shareholders," he said.
